# Antenatal corticosteroids for preterm babies

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Indicator ID | `neo_antenatal_steroids_preterm` |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Status | Draft |
| Unit | Neonatal |
| Type | Process |
| Direction | Higher is better |
| Table | `qi.qi_neonatal_antenatal_steroids_preterm`, one row per site and admission month |

## Definition

The share of babies born at 24 to 33 weeks of gestation whose mothers were recorded as receiving antenatal corticosteroids before delivery.

## Numerator

Eligible babies whose mothers were recorded as given antenatal corticosteroids. Column: `steroids_given`.

## Denominator

Babies with a gestation of 24 to 33 weeks, whatever their outcome. Column: `eligible`.

## Exclusions

- Babies under 24 weeks, outside the window in which WHO recommends antenatal corticosteroids.
- Gestations outside 22 to 46 weeks (likely typing errors) and missing gestations, which cannot decide eligibility. Both are counted and reported.
- Admissions without a usable admission date.

## Documentation completeness

The share of eligible babies with the antenatal corticosteroids question answered, yes or no (steroids_recorded / eligible). Not documented counts as not given.

## Breakdowns

- Place of birth: inborn (the admitting hospital cared for the mother), born outside the facility, or not recorded. Inborn babies reflect the hospital's own maternity care.

## REDCap fields

`mother_anten_corti`, `gest`, `bba`, `date_adm`, `hosp_id`

## Why it matters

Antenatal corticosteroids given to women at risk of preterm birth reduce neonatal death and respiratory distress in babies born early. The indicator links maternity care to newborn outcomes. WHO recommends them only when certain conditions are met (gestational age reliably assessed, birth imminent, no maternal infection, adequate care for mother and newborn), so 100% is not the expected target; trends and the inborn breakdown matter more than the level.
